fluff.overview: The Sojourner is a sixty-ton Clan OmniMech introduced in 3147 by Assault Tech Industries on Donegal, designed to serve the rebuilding Clan Wolf-in-Exile as an affordable and easily maintained frontline platform. Conceived during the post-Jihad era as a simple, cost-effective OmniMech to address persistent gaps in the Exiled Wolf touman, the design spent decades in virtual development before finally reaching a production line. The Sojourner prioritizes quantity and ease of repair over cutting-edge performance, making it one of the few Clan OmniMechs fielded extensively by both a Clan touman and an Inner Sphere military through production-sharing agreements with the Lyran Commonwealth.
fluff.capabilities:
Built around a Type W4 Endo Steel frame and protected by ten and a half tons of Compound RSH5 Ferro-Fibrous armor, the Sojourner prioritizes durability and simplicity over raw performance. The use of a standard Pitban 240 fusion engine rather than an extralight design reduces top speed to 64 kilometers per hour but keeps costs low and simplifies field repairs. A fixed Supercharger mounted on the chassis provides emergency bursts up to 86 kilometers per hour, intended primarily to allow inexperienced pilots to disengage from unfavorable engagements rather than to facilitate aggressive maneuvers.

The Sojourner dedicates 25.5 tons to pod space, with configurations built around a simple combat philosophy. An Actuator Enhancement System in the right arm serves as the primary weapons mount, while secondary armament is typically placed in the opposite torso, streamlining targeting solutions through the RCA Instatrac Mark XXII system. The Prime configuration exemplifies this approach, mounting a Gauss rifle in the enhanced right arm with an ER large laser and plasma cannon in the left torso, supplemented by jump jets and protected by a CASE II system that ensures combat survivability even if the Gauss rifle detonates.

Decades of virtual refinement have produced an OmniMech that is as easy to repair as it is to pilot, earning the Sojourner a reputation for returning damaged machines and their pilots to service with remarkable speed. This survivability, however, carries a double-edged consequence: Sojourners abandoned on the battlefield are just as easily salvaged and maintained by opposing forces.
fluff.history:
The Sojourner's journey from draft to production line is a study in Clan pragmatism born from necessity. Originally conceived during the relative stability following the Jihad, the design was intended to address a persistent gap in the Exiled Wolf touman for a cost-effective training and garrison OmniMech. The Republic of the Sphere's arms-reduction treaties under Devlin Stone rendered the project politically untenable, and it was officially shelved. Unofficially, a succession of Exiled Wolf technician-caste members treated the Sojourner as a passion project, iterating on the design across decades of virtual simulation and testing.

The catalyst for the Sojourner's production came with the fall of Arc-Royal in 3146. Clan Wolf-in-Exile, shattered and diminished, relocated to Donegal under Lyran protection. Khan Miriam Shaw's order to retool an Assault Tech Industries line for the Sojourner reflected a stark reassessment of her Clan's position: the Exiles needed machines they could produce quickly, crew with green warriors, and repair without specialized parts. The decades of virtual development meant the Sojourner's shakedown trials were completed with unusual speed, and full production commenced in 3147.

Shaw deployed the Sojourner throughout her depleted clusters, and the design quickly proved its worth in the ongoing conflicts of the ilClan era. In 3148, the Exiled Wolves brought war to the Jade Falcons on the occupied world of Upano, where a Star of Sojourner Primes engaged a numerically superior Falcon force across a volcanic plain. The engagement demonstrated both the design's resilience and the effectiveness of its straightforward weapons configurations, with three of five Sojourners surviving despite being ambushed and fighting through hellish terrain conditions.

Under agreements between the Exiled Wolves and the Lyran Commonwealth, a percentage of Sojourner production is allocated to the LCAF. While the Exiles primarily assign Sojourners to their greenest warriors as training platforms, the Lyrans have taken a different approach, distributing them among seasoned troops in units like the Bolan Jaegers who can fully exploit the advantages of Clan-grade weaponry. The Wolf Empire has also acquired Sojourners through defectors from the Exiles, fielding them as a signal of continued kinship with their wayward brethren. The Jade Falcons have likewise salvaged examples from the battlefield, though whether they will integrate a design so at odds with their doctrine of aggressive superiority remains uncertain.
fluff.deployment: This variant configuration represents the Sojourner's core design philosophy of simplicity and effectiveness. A Gauss rifle mounted in the Actuator Enhancement System-equipped right arm provides devastating long-range firepower, supported by an ER large laser and plasma cannon in the left torso. Target Interlock Circuits simplify the firing solution for inexperienced pilots, while a CASE II system in the right arm protects the MechWarrior from catastrophic Gauss rifle ammunition explosions. Jump jets enhance tactical mobility, and two tons of Gauss ammunition with one ton of plasma rounds provide adequate endurance for extended engagements.
